transcription.notes: Single-page problem list of the 29th IYPT (2016), 17 problems (the catalogue inventory summary listed only 1–12 by name but states 17). No points, no time limit and no solutions are printed. Epigraph (Goethe), author list, selection committee and the electronic-signature box at the bottom are not transcribed as problem content; the graphic at the bottom right of the page (about [514, 799, 954, 968] permille) is the electronic-signature block, not a figure. "Calliper" and "Analyse" are British spellings, kept as printed.

problems.title: Invent yourself
problems.statement: Truly random numbers are a very valuable and rare resource. Design, produce, and test a mechanical device for producing random numbers. Analyse to what extent the randomness produced is safe against tampering.

solution.incompleteReason: The archive has no official solutions for this paper (IYPT problems are open research problems).

problems.title: Lagging Pendulum
problems.statement: A pendulum consists of a strong thread and a bob. When the pivot of the pendulum starts moving along a horizontal circumference, the bob starts tracing a circle which can have a smaller radius, under certain conditions. Investigate the motion and stable trajectories of the bob.

solution.incompleteReason: The archive has no official solutions for this paper (IYPT problems are open research problems).

problems.title: Acoustic Lens
problems.statement: Fresnel lenses with concentric rings are widely used in optical applications, however a similar principle can be used to focus acoustic waves. Design and produce an acoustic lens and investigate its properties, such as amplification, as a function of relevant parameters.

solution.incompleteReason: The archive has no official solutions for this paper (IYPT problems are open research problems).

problems.title: Super Ball
problems.statement: Throw a highly elastic ball into the space between two plates. The ball starts bouncing and under some circumstances can even be projected back to you. Investigate the motion of the ball and parameters influencing the motion, including the orientation of the plates.

solution.incompleteReason: The archive has no official solutions for this paper (IYPT problems are open research problems).

problems.title: Ultrahydrophobic Water
problems.statement: Set a dish filled with soapy water onto a loudspeaker or other vibrator. When it oscillates, it is possible to hold small droplets on its surface for a long time. Explain and investigate the phenomenon.

problems.title: Electric Honeycomb
problems.statement: Set a vertically oriented steel needle over a horizontal metallic plate. Place some oil onto the plate. If you apply constant high voltage between the needle and the plate, a cell structure appears on the surface of the liquid. Explain and investigate this phenomenon.

problems.title: Hot Water Fountain
problems.statement: Partially fill a Mohr pipette with hot water. Cover the top of the pipette with your thumb. Turn the tip upwards and observe the fountain exiting the tip. Investigate the parameters describing the height of the fountain, and optimize them to get the maximum height.

problems.title: Magnetic Train
problems.statement: Button magnets are attached to both ends of a small cylindrical battery. When placed in a copper coil such that the magnets contact the coil, this "train" starts to move. Explain the phenomenon and investigate how relevant parameters affect the train's speed and power.

problems.title: Water Waves
problems.statement: Generate a water wave with a vertically oscillating horizontal cylinder. When varying the excitation frequency and/or amplitude, the water seems to drift away from or towards the cylinder. Investigate the phenomenon.

problems.title: Light Rings
problems.statement: Let a liquid jet fall onto a surface. If the contact point is illuminated by a laser beam, rings of light around the jet can be observed (see Figure). Investigate the light rings and determine how they depend on relevant parameters of the whole system.

problems.title: Rolling on a Disc
problems.statement: If you put a light rolling object (e.g. a ring, a disc, or a sphere) on a horizontal rotating disc, it may start moving without being expelled from the disc. Explain how different types of motion depend on the relevant parameters.

problems.title: Van der Pauw Method
problems.statement: It is known that conductivity of a material can be measured independently of the sample shape, as long as the sample has one border (no holes). To what extent can such a method be applied? Investigate and explain such measurements if the sample has holes.

problems.title: Paper Vice
problems.statement: Take two similar paperback books and interleave a few pages at a time. Push the books together. Hold the two books by their spines and try to pull them apart. Investigate the parameters that set the limits of being able to separate the books.

problems.title: Sensitive Flame
problems.statement: A combustible gas (e.g. propane) streams vertically out of a fine nozzle and then through a fine metallic mesh at a distance of about 5 cm. The gas is lit and produces a flame above the mesh. Under some circumstances, this flame reacts very sensitively to sound. Investigate the phenomenon and the relevant parameters.

problems.statement: Invent and construct an optical device that uses a laser pointer and allows contactless determination of thickness, refractive index, and other properties of a glass sheet.

problems.title: Frisbee Vortices
problems.statement: When a vertical plate is partially submerged in water and pulled in a direction normal to the plate, a pair of vortices is created in the surface of the water. Under certain conditions, these vortices travel along the surface for a long distance. Investigate the parameters influencing the motion and stability of these vortices.

problems.statement: When one pulls along a two wheeled suitcase, it can under certain circumstances wobble so strongly from side to side that it can turn over. Investigate this phenomenon. Can one suppress or intensify the effect by varied packing of the luggage?
